findings.finding: Cleveland-Cliffs printed Q3 this morning inside the window: adjusted EBITDA USD 612m against USD 286m in Q2, average net selling price USD 1,177/net ton (+USD 53, about +5% q/q), shipments 4.15m tons (+3%), adjusted EPS USD 0.28 against a USD 0.24 consensus, and it guided Q4 adjusted EBITDA to about USD 715m on 'increased pricing' with 2027 adjusted EBITDA above USD 4bn; CLF was +15.9% at 13:23 ET while STLD was +1.2%, so the read-through to STLD's own Q4 commentary tonight (flat-rolled pricing up again in Q4, imports low, lead times extended) is only partly transmitted.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: STLD does not give numeric Q4 guidance at the Q3 print (the Q4 guide comes in a mid-December 8-K); its qualitative outlook moved the stock +5.18% to the next close in April 2026 and +1.31% in July 2026 (OptionSlam trend page). The September mid-quarter guide, which is where the numbers land, cost about 5%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had carried the peer's Q4 pricing guide across, STLD would be up several percent on a day its closest flat-rolled peer is up 16%; it is up 1.2% at midday, the sector move is hours old, and Barclays' same-day target raise to USD 285 (stockanalysis news list, 2026-10-19) is the only sell-side reaction visible. The window starts at today's close, so whatever is transmitted by 16:00 ET is in the entry price and only the remainder is unpriced. Caveat already in the size: about half of CLF's move is CLF-specific (debt reduction, auto contract repricing, Stelco), and CLF is a far higher-beta, more heavily shorted name.
findings.independence: Proxy, not STLD's own number. Pointing the same way from a different source: Nucor's weekly HRC consumer spot price rose USD 10 a week from USD 1,190 on 2026-09-08 to USD 1,230 in the 2026-10-05 letter (GMK Center, https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-has-raised-the-price-of-hot-rolled-coils-to-1-230-per-tonne/), and Commercial Metals' FQ4 beat on 2026-10-15 (adjusted EPS 2.09 vs about 1.99, https://www.quiverquant.com/news/COMMERCIAL+METALS+%28%24CMC%29+Releases+Q4+2026+Earnings).

findings.finding: The flat-rolled spot price has kept rising through the quarter boundary: SMU's US HRC average was USD 1,205/st on 2026-09-01, Nucor's CSP went USD 1,190 (09-08) to 1,200 (09-15) to 1,230 (10-05 letter, +USD 10 every week, lead times 3-5 weeks) and Kallanish put spot at USD 1,210-1,220/st on 2026-10-02; STLD's realised steel price was USD 1,298/ton in Q2 and the September 8-K said Q3 realised prices rose while scrap fell, so the index-lagged contract book and spot both point to Q4 metal spread at least holding, against an implied Q4 consensus of about USD 5.28-5.39 that is flat on Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing commentary is the line this name trades on at the Q3 print; +5.18% in April 2026 when prices were rising into the call, +1.31% in July 2026 when the same message was already in the mid-quarter guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The weekly letters are public and the stock has recovered 11% from its 1 October low, so most of this is in the price; what is not is the Q4 read, because the sell-side's full-year numbers imply a flat Q4 and JPMorgan cut its target to USD 260 (Neutral) around 2026-10-09 (stockanalysis news list). If the market had extrapolated the weekly path into Q4, the Q4 consensus would sit above Q3 rather than level with it.
findings.independence: Industry series, not STLD's own number. CLF's Q4 guide (finding 1) is the direct counterparty confirmation; the two findings share the pricing thesis but rest on different documents. Caveat: October scrap settlement could not be found (Fastmarkets reported its Chicago busheling assessment delayed by late settlement on 2026-10-09, https://www.fastmarkets.com/?p=137741), so the cost side of the Q4 spread is unverified.

findings.finding: The reported quarter lands inside the company's own 2026-09-17 guide of USD 5.34-5.38 while consensus sits at USD 5.40-5.42 and the whisper at 5.47, so a print at the guide midpoint is a 1% miss to the estimate pages; metals recycling was guided lower (lower spreads, modestly lower shipments) and fabrication only 'modestly' better, so the beat has to come from steel, which was already guided to record shipments and margin expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: EPS 2.74 vs 2.63, stock -3.42% on the report day and +1.45% the next session (247wallst, https://247wallst.com/companies/stld/earnings/2025/Q3); Q2 2026: 3.69 vs 3.68-3.69, +1.31% to the next close; Q4 2025 (bmo): beat on EPS, missed revenue, about -2.4% intraday. The reported quarter has moved this name 1-3%, and a pre-guided quarter less.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is five weeks old and the stock fell about 5% on it, so the level is priced; what is not quite priced is that the estimate pages never came down to the guide (Zacks 5.42 against a 5.36 midpoint), which leaves a mechanical 1% 'miss' headline on the tape tonight.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers consensus 5.42 / whisper 5.47 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/STLD) and Tradestie 5.40 (https://tradestie.com/news/stld-earnings-oct-19-540-eps-consensus-key-levels-to-watch-20261019/) agree on the bar from different feeds.

findings.finding: Steel fabrication backlog was 'nearly 50 percent higher than prior-year third quarter levels' in the September 8-K against 'nearly 45 percent higher than a year ago' in the July release, both extending into Q1 2027, so the joist and deck book grew through Q3 while prices on it rose; Commercial Metals' 2026-10-15 fiscal Q4 beat on North America Steel growth corroborates non-residential demand into the fourth quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fabrication is about USD 85m of USD 700m quarterly operating income (Q2 2026 release), so it has not moved the stock on its own; it reads into the Q4 commentary rather than the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Both backlog figures were in the wire; the sequential rise from 45% to 50% is a comparison nobody has written up, and the Q2 fabrication margin compressed on steel input cost, so the market expects flat fabrication earnings while a bigger, higher-priced backlog says otherwise. Net of the rest of the company: steel is 10x the segment and is the line the stock moves on, so this is sized at a fraction of a pricing finding.
findings.independence: Prior release with the 45% figure: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926085277/tm2620920d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-07-20). CMC's print: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000053/cmc-8312026xearningsreleas.htm (2026-10-15).

findings.finding: Aluminum: the Columbus segment lost USD 33m in Q2 on 53,000 metric tons (Q1: 22,500 t, loss 48% larger), Q3 was guided to 'improve meaningfully' on shipments, all three cold mills are operational, the first CASH line is to ship commercial material in Q4 and the second to start customer-qualification material before year-end, with automotive sales expected before year-end; tonight's release is the first to show whether the segment loss has halved again toward breakeven or whether the Q4 commercial dates slipped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The USD 16m relocation impairment in July was absorbed inside a +1.31% day; the segment has not been the line the stock trades on, but a timing slip on the CASH lines would be new.
findings.why_not_priced: The qualitative ramp is in the wire; the number is not, and the full-year 2026 consensus range of USD 13.12-18.22 (stockanalysis) is wide enough that the aluminum loss trajectory is where the dispersion sits. If the market had a view it would show as a tighter range.
findings.independence: CRU Aluminum Market Update on the July ramp (third cold mill commissioning in July, auto sales before year-end): https://www.aluminummarketupdate.crugroup.com/growth-markets/adi-expects-auto-sales-from-mississippi-mill-to-begin-before-year-end/. Two-sided finding; sized near zero on purpose.

findings.finding: Buybacks ran USD 261m in Q3 to 2026-09-17 ('just under one percent' of shares) against USD 200m in all of Q2 and USD 315m in the first half, so the repurchase pace roughly doubled into the print; the full-quarter figure and any authorisation comment land tonight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback totals have not moved this stock on their own in the rebuilt set; they are a floor, not a catalyst.
findings.why_not_priced: The quarter-to-date number was in the 8-K the stock fell on; the step-up in pace against Q2 was not the headline of that day and is not in any preview read.
findings.independence: Q2 figure from the July release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926085277/tm2620920d1_ex99-1.htm. Shares the September document with findings 3, 4 and 5.

baseline_tension: The sealed baseline failed, so there is no skew or run-up to cut against; rebuilt, the stock is +11% off its 1 October low and 1.5% under its pre-guide peak with light short interest, and a mildly positive lean on a strong sector day agrees with that tape rather than beating it.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a proxy is filed smaller, not left out): the Cleveland-Cliffs read-through is a peer's number, not STLD's; finding 1 cut from +1.5 to +1.2 and p_up from 58 to 57, applied once.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the Q3 bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate pages, so no cap on the reported-quarter finding; the Q4 bar is derived by subtraction from two full-year consensus figures and the Benzinga mirrors disagree, so the guidance-line findings were kept small as already drafted.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest 3.0% of float, 3.8 DTC, no baseline skew; nothing to shrink on a positive lean.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): fabrication and aluminum findings were already sized net of the steel segment being 10x their size; unchanged.

The 'reaction history built from the wrong events' line: the base rate was rebuilt from OptionSlam and 247wallst rows for Jul-26, Apr-26, Jan-26 and Oct-25 before sizing abs_move_pct, as the sweep asked; unchanged by the file.
